nodes.title: Model download links
widgets_values:
Download either the fp8 or the gguf version of the model. If you have limited VRAM, gguf is recommended.

The Q5 version is a good middleground between size and quality.

widgets_values: A man stands at the edge of a crumbling concrete walkway, looking down into a massive sinkhole filled with bubbling, churning lava. He slowly raises his arms outward for balance as the ground beneath him cracks and shifts. Small chunks of asphalt break off and fall into the glowing molten pit below. Embers and sparks drift upward around him. He takes one cautious step backward, glancing left and right nervously. The lava pulses and glows deep orange and red, casting flickering light across his face and chest. Office buildings and parked cars sit calmly in the background, untouched, creating an eerie contrast with the apocalyptic ground below. Bare birch trees line the right side. Midday light. Cinematic, realistic VFX, wide angle.

- frames_per_iteration = Number of frames generated per iteration. Must follow the Wan formula: 4n+1 (e.g. 41, 45, 49, 53, 57, 61, 65, 69, 73, 77, 81).

- num_start_frames = Number of frames carried over from the previous iteration as context for the current one.

- resume_from_iteration = Resume generation from a specific iteration, keeping all previously accumulated frames. Useful for trying different seeds on later iterations without re-running the entire workflow. Set to 0 to start over from scratch.

- total_iterations = Total number of iterations to run. You can start with a lower value, check the result, and then increase it later using resume_from_iteration to continue where you left off.

- mode = Controls start image behavior. All images are always used as reference.
    - Start + Reference: First image also used as start image.
    - Reference: No start image.
    - Auto: Enables start image with 1 image, disables with more than 1.

- match_mode = Selects how the generated VFX is processed before output:
    - Disabled (pass-through): Outputs the generated video unchanged.
    - Color Match: Matches the video to the first generation. Only works from the second iteration on.
    - Compose + Match: Composites the VFX based on the mask and matches its grading to the plate.
  (heavier)
! You can finetune the COLOR MATCH / COMPOSE SETTINGS inside the subgraph in the purple group section !

nodes.title: CLIP Text Encode (Positive Prompt)
widgets_values: Water suddenly rushes in from the right side of the frame, pouring through the windows and surging across the flooded office floor. The incoming current pushes existing standing water to the left, creating turbulent ripples and small waves that splash against the desk legs and chair base. The water level rises steadily as the flow continues from the right side of the screen, climbing up the furniture. Foam and churning white water form at the leading edge of the surge. Reflections on the water surface distort and shimmer with the turbulence. The man in the jeans with grey sneakers is dodging the water. Fixed lens, low angle. Photorealistic, natural daylight, volumetric mist above water surface.

COMPOSE + MATCH (per-frame)
  Composites SOURCE over DESTINATION via MASK and fixes the seam where they meet.

  Wiring (insert a regenerated element back over original footage):
  • source      = regenerated frame (e.g. WAN) with the new element
  • destination = original / untouched footage (the plate)
  • mask        = white where you keep the source

  correction:
  • Grade match (surround) ← default. Measures the VAE grading drift from the area
    OUTSIDE the mask (same scene in both) and applies it to the element INSIDE.
    The element keeps its colors (lava stays lava); only its grading matches the plate.
  • Color match (palette) = palette match — tints the element toward the scene. Off = plain comp.

  Key knobs:
  • strength      amount of correction (1 = full)
  • grade_fit     Gain+offset = luminance + contrast / Offset only = milder
  • surround_band 0 = whole surround / >0 = ring around mask if drift varies
  • saturation    undo VAE flatness (~1.1–1.3)
  • black_point   undo milky lifted blacks (~0.01–0.03)
  • edge_falloff  feather the trims inward so they don't make a new seam (~8–24 px)
